name: bank_lines
title: Bank Lines
description: Imported statement lines -- the independent third-party record the books are checked against, and the reason bank reconciliation is the #1 practical anti-fraud control. Append-only and never hand-edited: `raw` keeps the original row verbatim forever and the parsed fields are a VIEW of it, so nobody can quietly 'fix up' the evidence to agree with the books. amount_cents is signed (money into the account positive, out negative). Everything an operator DOES with a line -- matching it, resolving it as a fee or a transfer -- is a separate attributed update, so who reconciled what and when is structural, which matters because reconciliation performed invisibly by the same hands that move money is the classic fraud hole. hooks.before_write rejects duplicates within an account (external_id when the bank gives one, else line_hash).

fields.name: amount_cents
fields.label: Amount (cents)
fields.help: Signed: positive is money into the account, negative is money out. Integer cents, never a float.

fields.name: external_id
fields.label: Bank Transaction ID
fields.help: The bank's own id (OFX FITID) when the format carries one -- the strongest dedup key.

fields.name: line_hash
fields.label: Line Hash
fields.help: Content hash used for dedup when the bank gives no id; ordinal-disambiguated so genuine same-day twins both land.

fields.name: raw
fields.label: Raw Row
fields.help: The original statement row, verbatim. Never rewritten -- this is the evidence.

fields.name: match_status
fields.label: Match Status
fields.help: unmatched -> suggested (the matcher proposed something) -> matched (a human confirmed) or resolved (booked as a fee/interest/transfer/NSF/timing item). Every move is attributed.

fields.name: matched_to
fields.label: Matched To
fields.help: collection/record_id of the book-side record this line is, e.g. payments/p1 or fin_journals/j9.

fields.name: resolved_as
fields.label: Resolved As
fields.help: For lines with no book counterpart yet: what the line actually was. Each has a resolution verb that composes the right journal.

fields.name: suggestions
fields.label: Suggestions (JSON)
fields.help: What the matcher proposed and why (tier + candidates). Derived and non-authoritative -- a human confirmation is what writes matched_to.
